entry.title: Enabling RS Drive 2 in a Megane MK3

link.title: Enabling RS Drive 2 in a Megane MK3

entry.content:
I don’t know why, but some cars that have RS Monitor don’t have RS Drive 2 enabled, which basically allows you to change throttle response, traction control, and the engine map per mode, Normal, Sport and Race. This is a guide on how to enable that via DDT4ALL.

There aren’t any English guides on this so I thought I’d make one, it’s actually very easy to do.

First you’ll need a modified ELM327 adapter like this one designed for Ford as they use the same pinout as Renault. For this to work you’ll need the driver which you can download here, just plug in the ELM and install the driver. Then you’ll need DDT4ALL, download the latest release for your system. At the time of writing this I was using 3.1.3. DDT4ALL doesn’t ship with database files, here’s database files from February 2021, just unzip and place all of the folders/files into the DDT4ALL install folder.

Once you have DDT4ALL setup we need to go over to the car and plug in the ELM adapter to the OBD port and the laptop. Make sure the ignition is on (just put the key in the slot) and then run DDT4ALL. Make sure you accept the disclaimer and then select Connected mode.

You’ll also need to make sure that the adapter is in the correct mode to communicate with the infotainment system rather than engine computer. On the adapter I linked above when it’s plugged in and the sticker is facing up, the metal switch should be in the down position. If for whatever reason the next steps don’t show the correct results just flip it and try again.

As below, select “[X95PH2] - Renault Megane III Ph2” from the dropdown, it will work without doing this however the next step will take a lot longer as it will search for every single ECU, not just the Megane III ones.

Then press scan button to the right of the drop down menu, it looks like a QR code with a magnifying glass next to it and wait, it should take a couple of minutes to scan.

Once the scan has finished you should see some ECUs appear in the Ecu window below, the one we’re looking for should be named “MFD v5.4” or something very similar.

Once you click on “MFD v5.4” you’ll see some new options appear below in Screen window, expand “1 - Configuration”, then select “14 - ECU configuration - HMI.TMPS,RestrictionVIN,RS Display & Communication”. As seen below.

As you can see above the main window should contain a bunch of red, green and yellow boxes. Scroll down until we get to “RS DISPLAY” with 3 options below it. The one we are interested in is “RS Configuration Slot 1”. Slot 2 isn’t needed for what we’re doing.

Before we go any further I highly suggest you copy and save Slot 1 and 2 (even though we’re not touching 2, it’s good practice) somewhere safe just in case the edit goes wrong so you have your original figures. You copy from the red boxes on the left, it won’t let you copy from the right side.

On another note, if anyone follows this guide on a Megane 265, can you please comment your Slot 1 and 2 figures below as I’ve not come across those yet, and I’ll add them here.

I’ll be using a Megane 275 slot as an example. Below is the original Megane 275 slot 1 with two modified ones (the first one just enables RS Drive, the second one enables RS Drive but also makes other readouts a lot more useful like coolant temp and oil temp, as it lowers the values needed to display them. For example normally oil doesn’t display until 50C, but with this it displays from 0C). I’ll also add slot 2 just in case anyone needs or wants it, but we don’t need it for this.

RS 275 Slot 1: 

RS 275 Slot 1 RS Drive: 

RS 275 Slot 2: 

If you look, only the last part of the slot is changed, this tells the car to enable RS Drive.

Make sure that these two buttons are pressed at the top of DDT4ALL, “Expert mode” and “Auto refresh”. Expert mode allows writing to the ECU, and auto refresh just reads the ECU automatically which makes it easier to know if your write worked.

Now just copy and paste one of the modified slot 1 codes from above and paste it over the contents in “RS Configuration Slot 1” (or clear the box first) and then press “Write RS Slot1”, it will be hard to tell but the contents of the green box should also change.

At this point it should be done, I had to disconnect the battery on my car for it to appear. You may be able to just leave the car for a few hours, or try pressing the home button 5 times quickly which reboots the screen, but I didn’t try this.

Now you can access RS Drive from within RS Monitor and change settings from there.

For anyone that’s interested in what slot 2 does, it basically manages the torque and power graphs in RS Monitor, changing these does not change the map on the car, its for display only. On a standard car you don’t need to change these but on a mapped/modified one you can change this to reflect the real power of the car as I have done on my Megane RS400.

For anyone wanting to do this, here is a spreadsheet which allows you to input new figures and generates a new code for you. If you do this you also need to edit slot 1 again with the new peak power and torque figures.

Disclaimer: This guide is provided for information only, and you follow it entirely at your own risk. Writing to your car’s ECUs can cause unexpected behaviour, and I can’t be held responsible for any damage to your vehicle, loss of data or warranty, or anything else that results. These steps worked for me on my own car, but that’s no guarantee they’ll work on yours. Always back up your original slot values before changing anything, and if you’re not comfortable doing this yourself, speak to a professional.
entry.summary: A guide on enabling RS Drive 2 in RS Monitor on a Renault Megane MK3 with a R-Link infotainment system.

entry.title: AMDGPU Issues on Kernel 7.1.6, 7.1.7, and 7.1.8
entry.content:
In recent Fedora kernel updates, specifically 7.1.6 and 7.1.7, regressions in the amdgpu driver broke display output and caused crashes for a lot of AMD GPU users, along with weird graphical artifacts. The best thing to do for now is boot into kernel 7.1.5, remove the broken builds, and temporarily exclude them in DNF.

7.1.8 has fixed some of the issues but still isn’t 100% there so I’d still suggest going to 7.1.5.

First, reboot your system, select 7.1.5 from the GRUB boot menu, and make sure you’re running it:

uname -r

Once booted into .5, remove the broken kernel releases:

sudo dnf remove "kernel*7.1.6*" "kernel*7.1.7*" "kernel*7.1.8*"

To prevent Fedora from pulling 7.1.6, 7.1.7, or 7.1.8 back down during your next update, edit your DNF config:

sudo nano /etc/dnf/dnf.conf

Add this line under the [main] section:

excludepkgs=kernel*7.1.6* kernel*7.1.7* kernel*7.1.8*

Save and exit.

This will block 7.1.6, 7.1.7, and 7.1.8 from reinstalling while keeping you open to receive kernel 7.1.9 or newer as soon as a fix lands.
entry.summary: Recent 7.1.6, 7.1.7 and 7.1.8 kernel releases caused amdgpu driver issues. Here is how to roll back to 7.1.5 and pin it.

entry.title: Retrofit Sunvisor Lights to Renault Megane MK3

link.title: Retrofit Sunvisor Lights to Renault Megane MK3

entry.content:
This is pretty unnecessary, but it was the only option now missing from my car. So I decided to retrofit it and make a guide just in case anyone else wanted to do it.

First you need to check if you have the correct sun visors, from my research it seems that some cars have them installed already even if you don’t have the lights, my passenger side one was already correct but the driver’s side was not. You can identify this quite easily by removing the sunvisor from the headlining and looking for these two pins here.

Then you need the sunvisor lights and loom, the loom looks complicated but we won’t actually be using it all, unless you want to pull out the whole headliner and A pillars, go for it, but I don’t. We’ll just be cutting off the 4 plugs we need and getting power from the dome light. The lights are used on more than just the Megane, they’re also in the Scenic, and Laguna from what I’ve seen, maybe even the Clio too.

I want this loom to be removable, so we’re going to use these plugs which are readily available from eBay or Amazon, or your local hardware store.

There are a few ways you could connect this, we just need power and ground, you could solder this directly to the dome power and ground pads, or splice it into the loom going to it, either way is fine.

Here’s the loom we’ve made, it’s 5 plugs in total. 2 go to each sun visor to tell the lights when to turn on and off, 2 go to the lights and then the other one is to connect this to our existing loom in the headliner where we’re getting our power from.

It’s pretty simple, power comes from the dome light straight to the light, the ground wire runs through the sunvisor plug, that way it’s only grounded when the sunvisor mirror is open, allowing the light to get power.

You need to use pins 2 and 4 for the power off of the dome light. Pin 2 always gets 12v when the ignition is on, pin 4 is ground. If you use pin 1 or 3 the lights will work, but only when the dome light is on.

We’ve done most of the work now, all that’s left is to fit it all which requires cutting a small hole in the headlining for our new light, you can see the hole I cut below. Below is a picture of a Megane 3 with no headliner in, so you can see the holes where the sunvisor mounts to and also the hole for the wiring the sunvisor light will come through, so although it doesn’t really matter where you put it, as the light just mounts to the headliner and not the roof of the car, I would aim for around there. I would trace around the light on a bit of paper and then cut that paper smaller than the tracing by about 5mm all the way around and then trace around that paper on the headliner. I’d use a new Stanley blade so it’s sharp and go slowly.

Now all there is to do is fit it all, I’d start with the loom, get it all into position and dangle the plugs through the holes needed, plug it into wherever you wired our 2 pin plug in, then plug in the light and clip it into place. Plug in the sunvisor and clip that back into place, and give it all a test by opening the sunvisor mirror cover.

Disclaimer: This guide is provided for information only, and you follow it entirely at your own risk. This job involves splicing into your car’s electrical system and cutting into the headlining. Disconnect the battery before working on any wiring, and be aware that airbag components and their wiring run close to the headlining and A pillars on many cars, so take care and check your car’s service information before cutting or removing anything. Incorrect wiring can cause electrical faults, blown fuses or fire, and a badly cut headlining can’t easily be undone. I can’t be held responsible for any damage to your vehicle, injury, loss of warranty, or anything else that results.
entry.summary: A guide on retrofitting sunvisor lights to a Renault Megane MK3.

entry.title: Windows System Reserved Partition Update Error

link.title: Windows System Reserved Partition Update Error

entry.content:
Windows 10 and 11 have a fault with Windows update, causing the following error - Windows couldn’t be installed, we couldn’t update the System Reserved Partition with the error code 0xc1900104, 0x800f0922, 0x800f0922 or 0xc1900201.

The issue is caused by the System Reserved Partition running out of space, as this partition is very small by design and can be filled up by updates, or some anti-virus apps also write to it. There are two fixes, the first is expanding that partition which is a lot of work, so option two is the better option.

You need to free up about 10-15MB of space on that partition, so not much at all.

Open command prompt or terminal as an adminstrator and run the following commands:

Mount the System Reserved Partition as Y:

mountvol y: /s

Change to the Y: partition

Y:

Change the current directory to the fonts directory

cd EFI\Microsoft\Boot\Fonts

Then delete all of the files in that directory

del *.*

This will delete all of the fonts with that folder and free up enough space to complete Windows updates.
entry.summary: Fix the Windows 10/11 system reserved partition update error, causing Windows to not update

entry.title: Docker 29 API Changes
entry.content:
In the latest Docker release, version 29, they increased the minimum API version which broken a lot of containers. The best thing to do for now is not update, but if like me you already did, you could either downgrade or just add the following to your docker.service file.

sudo systemctl edit docker.service

Add this part above the line _### Lines below this comment will be

[Service]
Environment=DOCKER_MIN_API_VERSION=1.24

Save and exit

sudo systemctl restart docker

This will force docker to use the old API version as it was before.
entry.summary: Docker 29 recently upgraded the minimum API version, which broke a lot of stuff

entry.title: Bypass Windows 11 Microsoft Account Requirement
entry.content:
Since the introduction of Windows 11, Microsoft haave forced users to create or login to a Microsoft account during a new installation. This can be very annoying if you don’t want a Microsoft account, or are setting up the computer for someone else, like we do everyday.

You used to be able open command prompt by using Shift+F10 (Shift+Fn+F10 on some laptops) and type the following command.

taskkill /F /IM oobenetworkconnectionflow.exe

Since 24H2 this no longer works, strangely I’ve found it works very occasionally.

The new method is as follows, don’t connect to any wireless network, if you have ethernet then just unplug the cable. When you get to the stage of being asked for a Microsoft account, open command, press Shift+F10 (Shift+Fn+F10 on some laptops) and type the following

start ms-cxh:localonly

this will bypass the online account and allow you to create a local user with or without a password.
entry.summary: Bypass the need for a Microsoft account during Windows 11 installation

entry.title: Retrofit Powerfold Mirrors Renault Megane MK3

link.title: Retrofit Powerfold Mirrors Renault Megane MK3

entry.content:
It annoyed me that my RS didn’t have folding mirrors, so I retrofit them. There isn’t, or wasn’t any info on doing this at the time I did it, so I decided to make a guide.

First of all, you need to check if you have the correct looms. Mine did but I’m not sure if all models do or only RS models. Take this panel off on both sides.

Now you can check the loom for the correct wire.

If you have the correct loom then you just need to get new mirrors and the driver’s window switch controls.

I’ve circled the pin you need to look for on each mirror to make sure they’re electric folding compared to a non-folding version.

Once you’ve swapped the mirrors it will require coding with either CLIP or DDT4ALL, I’ve not used CLIP so the tutorial will be with DDT.

You need to get a special adapter used on Fords as Renault and Ford share an OBD2 pinout. You can get them on eBay for around a tenner. Search Ford ELM327 on eBay and you should find a USB to OBD2 adapter.

Install DDT4ALL, link to the software and some databases.

I’m not going to go through a complete tutorial on how to use the software, if you need to learn then use this guy on YouTube, he’s not English but you can still follow along pretty easily.

You need to go to DDCM > Driver DCM X95 SLOT v4.0 > DCM Configuration > Write Configuration Select the correct options for your car and then press send

If you get an error that you need expert mode it’s the second option along the top, the weird black and white face and make sure your ignition is on but the engine is not.

I’m happy to help anyone if you can’t get it working, just send me an email at info@professorshroom.com.

Disclaimer: This guide is provided for information only, and you follow it entirely at your own risk. Writing coding changes to your car’s ECUs can cause unexpected behaviour, and I can’t be held responsible for any damage to your vehicle, loss of data or warranty, or anything else that results. These steps worked for me on my own car, but that’s no guarantee they’ll work on yours. Always back up your original configuration before changing anything, and if you’re not comfortable doing this yourself, speak to a professional.
entry.summary: A guide on retrofitting electric folding mirrors to Renault Megane MK3.

entry.title: Update Renault Megane MK3 Radio to 2.42 (Latest/Final Update)

link.title: Update Renault Megane MK3 Radio to 2.42 (Latest/Final Update)

entry.content:
The latest and last update for the standard Renault Megane MK3 headunit solves some issues with Bluetooth, so here’s a guide on how to do that.

First you need a USB stick formatted to FAT32.

Download this file and place it on the USB stick, make sure it’s the only file on it.

Plug the USB stick into your car and make sure the radio is on. I would start the engine to make sure the ignition doesn’t turn off during the process.

Switch the radio into FM mode.

Open settings which is the bottom right button on the radio and navigate to Audio Settings > USB connection version > Display the software version.

If it says anything other than “s2.42m2.42” then you need to update.

Open settings which is the bottom right button on the radio and navigate to Audio Settings > USB connection version > Update Software.

The update will take 1-2 minutes and then you’re done!

Disclaimer: This guide is provided for information only, and you follow it entirely at your own risk. Updating the firmware on your radio carries a risk of the unit failing to boot or becoming unusable if the update is interrupted, so make sure the engine is running or your battery is in good health before you start, and don’t turn anything off or remove the USB stick until it has finished. I can’t be held responsible for any damage to your radio, your car or your warranty.
entry.summary: A guide on updating radio/headunit in a Renault Megane MK3 to 2.42 which is the latest and final update.
